llm.summary: The code matches the described purpose (autonomous posting across X/Instagram/YouTube/Meta) but there are several coherence and safety concerns you should understand before installing.

dimensions.detail: The requested credentials (Twitter/X, Instagram Graph, Meta page token, YouTube OAuth, Cloudflare R2) align with the stated goal of fully autonomous posting and video hosting. However there are metadata inconsistencies: the registry listing claims no homepage/source while the bundled clawhub.json and README point to a GitHub repo, and some branding is hardcoded in the code (see below) despite SKILL.md saying placeholders should be replaced.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The SKILL.md instructs fully autonomous posting and the scripts do that (posting, commenting, uploading to R2, marking CSV rows as posted). Several surprising behaviors in the code: (1) hardcoded promotional/watermark strings (e.g., 'Mission UPSC Tracker' watermark and 'Download Mission UPSC from Playstore' banner) that will appear in generated content even though SKILL.md says to replace BRAND_URL/BRAND_NAME placeholders; (2) the code writes logs, creates output/log directories, and modifies the local CSV (mark_as_posted) — all expected but worth noting; (3) YouTube OAuth requires a client_secrets.json and browser flow; (4) the skill truly uploads generated video content to an external host (R2) and posts content externally. These are within scope, but the hardcoded branding/promo is an unexpected side effect and a coherence issue.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install spec in the package (no automatic installer). The SKILL.md lists many Python dependencies (tweepy, moviepy, boto3, google-api-python-client, etc.) which must be installed by the user. Lack of an install script is not dangerous but means manual setup is required and dependency management is left to you.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The environment variables requested (X/Twitter keys, INSTAGRAM_*, META_PAGE_*, R2_*, plus YouTube client_secrets.json) match the actions the skill performs (posting, uploads, OAuth). That said, the skill needs high-privilege posting credentials across multiple platforms simultaneously — this is necessary for the functionality but increases risk (account takeover/impersonation if keys are leaked).
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not marked always:true. It is capable of autonomous posting when invoked and will perform external network actions with the supplied credentials. Because it requires full posting credentials for multiple platforms, autonomous invocation (the platform default) has a higher blast radius — review and restrict agent autonomy if you need additional guardrails.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
Things to check before you install/use this skill:

- Only provide account credentials you are willing to let an autonomous agent fully control. Prefer test accounts or accounts with restricted access until you trust the skill.
- Review and remove/replace hardcoded branding and promotional text if you don't want 'Mission UPSC' and Playstore links embedded in every generated image/video (image_generator and video_generator contain hardcoded watermark/banner text). SKILL.md's placeholder instructions are not consistently applied in code.
- Confirm the repository/source/trustworthiness. The package metadata in this bundle contradicts the SKILL.md/README (registry says source/homepage unknown while clawhub.json/README point to a GitHub project). If origin is important, verify the upstream repository and maintainer.
- The skill uploads media to Cloudflare R2; verify R2 endpoint and use scoped keys and a dedicated bucket. Rotate keys after testing and consider using short-lived credentials where possible.
- Install dependencies in a controlled environment (virtualenv/container). Test in dry-run mode first (the scripts support dry-run) to ensure videos generate as expected and posting paths work.
- Because the agent can post and comment automatically, consider adding human approval or limiting agent autonomy until you are confident (the platform default allows autonomous invocation — not a defect of the skill, but a risk when combined with full posting credentials).

If you want a lower-risk trial: create separate test accounts for each platform, create a test R2 bucket and keys, run locally in --dry-run to verify outputs, and inspect generated media for any unwanted promotional text or leaks before connecting production credentials.
